reviews.title: The files inside the file
reviews.review: Retain list-first/no eager decode behavior. §7.11.4.1 says embedded streams need not be processed by every processor, and the list path should not inflate every attachment on document open. This does not waive a checksum assertion when the extraction path already has decoded bytes; ADR 0145 is the later owner for that path.

reviews.title: Taking a file out of a document
reviews.review: Retain checksum-at-extraction and host-owned writing. The Table45 checksum is over uncompressed data and explicitly not a security mechanism. Existing raw-payload assertions prove MD5 but do not distinguish decoding from checking compressed stream bytes; proposed embedded_flate_checksum.rs is a targeted public regression for the missing combination.

reviews.title: A link is a program this machine starts, so the reader says whether it may
reviews.review: The no-direct-opening boundary remains sound. The component-count finding concerns the value carried in ExternalData and its interpretation, not opening an arbitrary document-selected path; the host's separate one-component rule still decides what may be fetched.

reviews.title: The bytes a stream points at are the caller's to fetch
reviews.review: The archive transformation deliberately reuses FileSpec parsing, so string-grammar losses are observable in an actual report even though this model code does not open anything. `ExternalData::Named` carries both shown string and byte components/absolute bit. This makes the 256-component silent separator merge more than dead helper behavior, while the one-component host policy constrains actual fetches.

reviews.title: A panel is eleven answers, and none of them is a number
reviews.review: Relevant only as API scope: a confined host carries attachment metadata without the stream; extract events supply bytes later. The checksum predicate is intentionally a separate cross-boundary operation. The proposed regression stays inside pdf-model and checks decoded bytes available to the extraction consumer; it does not alter confined wire policy.
